thread.title: Facebook earnings: Stock touches record after massive ad price increase

author: morningstar.com
title: Facebook earnings: Stock touches record after massive ad price increase
text:
By Max A. Cherney
Average price for Facebook ads jumps 43% in fourth quarter
Facebook Inc. stock swung to a record in late trading Wednesday after the company reported double-digit advertising price growth during the company's fourth-quarter earnings call with investors.
After dropping more than 2% immediately after the company released its fourth-quarter earnings, Facebook shares (FB) swung as high as $194.50 during the earnings call as executives discussed ad pricing growth. Shares were last up about 1%, at $188.80. In prepared remarks, Chief Financial Officer David Wehner said that the average price per ad increased by 43%, and the total number of impressions -- pages loaded with ads served by Facebook -- jumped 4% last quarter.
More:Facebook stock heads for record after earnings show ad prices increasing: live blog recap (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/facebook-earnings-to-provide-insight-into-news-feed-changes-live-blog-2018-01-31)
"So you can think of all these ... optimization efforts as part of that as being an effort to improve the yield of the impressions that we have to drive downstream business results for our advertising partners," Wehner said on the call. "And if we can drive those effectively that will translate into higher effective prices for our business."
The majority of the pricing increase is due to Facebook's core app as well as Instagram, which it does not break out financial results for (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/the-youtube-and-instagram-secret-that-google-and-facebook-dont-want-you-to-know-2018-01-26).
Read:The YouTube and Instagram secret that Google and Facebook don't want you to know (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/the-youtube-and-instagram-secret-that-google-and-facebook-dont-want-you-to-know-2018-01-26)
Compared with the year-ago quarter, the number of impressions compared with ad price growth has flipped: In 2016's fourth quarter, impressions grew by 49% and ad prices went up by 3%. But since the beginning of 2017, Facebook's ad impression growth has decelerated incrementally from 32% in the first quarter, sending prices up.
The refrain is a familiar one to Facebook watchers -- as the amount of ad inventory grows more slowly and advertisers still hunger to spend dollars there, the price goes up. To wit, in 2015's first quarter, Facebook served 62% fewer impressions, sending ad prices up a whopping 285%.
Facebook is one of six companies that have topped a $500 billion (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/techs-500-billion-club-has-tripled-and-it-dominates-the-market-as-earnings-storm-approaches-2018-01-30) market valuation and are reporting results Wednesday and Thursday (the others are Alibaba Group Holding Ltd.(BABA), Google parent Alphabet Inc. (GOOGL) (GOOGL) , Amazon.com Inc. (AMZN) and Apple Inc. (AAPL)) . Microsoft Corp. (MSFT) , one of the six, also reported earnings Wednesday (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/shares-of-microsoft-slide-as-software-giant-reports-a-quarterly-loss-on-tax-cuts-2018-01-31).
Facebook stock has gained 43% in the past 12 months, with the S&P 500 index gaining 24% in that time.
-Max A. Cherney;
01-31-18 1918ET
